questions.hint: ARPANET was developed by ARPA (Advanced Research Projects Agency) of the U.S. government in 1969.

questions.ans: A computer network is a set of computers connected together for the purpose of sharing resources. The Internet is the most common resource shared today. Computer networking is a technique of digital telecommunication that permits nodes to share resources with one another. Data is exchanged as the main element. Links are transferred over cable media (optic cables, wires) or wireless media (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi).

questions.q: Write a short note on Internet.
questions.ans: Internet stands for INTERconnected NETwork. It is the connection of individual networks operated by academic, industry, government, and private parties. The Internet is a worldwide system of computer networks — a network of networks where users at any computer can get information from any other computer. It is connected by guided, wireless, and fiber-optic technologies. It was developed by ARPA of the U.S. government in 1969 (first known as ARPANet). Internet is a universal source of information for billions of people at work, at home, and at school.

questions.q: What are the common uses of computer networks?
questions.ans: The three common uses of computer networks are: 1. Communication — Using computer networks, people can interact with others across the world at very low cost via mobile, e-mail, chatting, video conferencing, SMS, and groupware. 2. Resource Sharing — Allows programs, equipment, and data to be accessed by anyone via the network regardless of physical location. Includes sharing printers, scanners, fax machines. 3. Information Sharing — Applications stored at a central server can be shared among all computers on the network. Provides high reliability and backup.

questions.q: What is a node in Computer Network?
questions.ans: A node is a computer which is connected to a network. Data originates and terminates at nodes. The data origin is called the source and the data destination is called the destination. In networking, nodes are identified by their IP addresses (network address). Nodes can include hosts such as mobile phones, tablets, personal computers, large servers, and other networking devices. Connecting more than one device together forms a network.

questions.q: Write a note on Resource Sharing in computer networks.
questions.ans: Resource sharing is one of the major uses of computer networks. It allows all kinds of programs, equipment, and data to be accessed by anyone via the network, irrespective of the physical location of the resource. Simply put, resource sharing means sharing of devices like printers, scanners, PDA, fax machines, and modems among multiple computers connected to a network. This eliminates the need for each computer to have its own separate printer or scanner — one device can be shared by many users. This reduces cost significantly and increases efficiency in offices and organizations.

questions.q: List out some benefits of social networks.
questions.ans:
Benefits of social networks:
1. Group information sharing over long distances — Friends and family can share photo albums, videos, and daily wishes through social networks, providing a richer environment than phone calls or text messages.
2. Broadcast announcements — Quick and easy way to spread information about emergencies, natural calamities, and upcoming events. Venues and businesses can advertise through social networks.
3. Content contribution — Networks allow members to easily share comments, audio, video, text, and animation files with others.
4. Frequent visits — Healthy social networks have active members who check in regularly to contribute and receive new updates.
5. Relationship building — Social networks allow interaction among people, creating stronger connections across different communities.

questions.q: Write a note on Mobile Networks.
questions.ans: A mobile network is a network connecting devices without cable (wireless). Mobile computers such as laptops, tablets, and handheld computers are the fastest growing segments. At land areas, the network is distributed as cells, each served by a single-location transceiver (base transceiver station). The base station provides network coverage for voice, data, and content transmission. Joining together all radio coverage creates a wide geographical area. Portable transceivers communicate with one another and with fixed transceivers, moving across more than one cell during transmission. Examples: mobiles, tablets, pagers, laptops with mobile broadband and dongles.

Computer networks play a major role in providing information to large and small organizations and common people. The three major uses are:

1. Communication:
Using computer networks, we can interact with people all over the world. People can communicate at very low cost via mobile, social media, telephone, e-mail, chatting, video conferencing, SMS, MMS, and groupware. This has made the world a smaller place.

2. Resource Sharing:
Allows all kinds of programs, equipment, and data to be accessed by anyone via the network irrespective of physical location. Resource sharing means sharing devices like printers, scanners, PDA, fax machines, and modems. This reduces duplication of equipment and saves cost.

3. Information Sharing:
Using computer networks, any application or software can be stored at a central computer or server and shared among other computers. It provides high reliability — backup can be stored at one location for easy availability in case of a crash.

Applications in specific areas:
- Business: E-banking, cloud computing, B2B/B2C/B2G transactions without geographical boundaries.
- Home: E-learning, e-governance, e-health, telemedicine, video conferencing.
- Mobile: Wireless connectivity via cells and base stations.
- Social: WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter for sharing thoughts, ideas, and files globally.

questions.q: Explain about social applications in Computer Networks.
questions.ans:
Social applications in computer networks connect people around the world through social network media. Applications like WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter, Blogs, Pinterest, and Classmate are in full use.

Common attributes of social networks:
1. Membership — Requires user registration with names and accounts. Public networks offer free registration; private networks restrict membership.
2. Content contribution — Members can share comments, audio, video, text, and animation files.
3. Frequent visits — Active members check in regularly for new updates.
4. Relationship building — Creates stronger connections among people of different communities.

Benefits of social networks:
1. Group information sharing — Share photo albums, videos, and wishes over long distances.
2. Broadcast announcements — Spread information about emergencies and events quickly.
3. Fostering diversity of thought — People of different opinions connect and discuss.

Disadvantages of social networks:
1. Wasting precious time on surfing and searching unwanted content.
2. Unnecessary wrong information posted on web pages and blogs.
3. Different types of theft related to money and valuables through hackers and viruses.

When people of different opinions get together online, discussions can lead to personal attacks — called flame wars.
